links.title: Automate the Boring Stuff with Python, 3rd edition: Chapter 22, Recognizing Text in Images
links.why: The course textbook's own chapter, free online: installing Tesseract, the four lines, preprocessing, language models, languages, NAPS2 and the practice program.

links.title: pytesseract 0.3.13 on PyPI
links.why: The functions PyTesseract offers besides image_to_string: image_to_data, image_to_boxes, image_to_pdf_or_hocr, config, lang and timeout.

links.title: Tesseract User Manual: Improving the quality of the output
links.why: The engine's own advice on rescaling, binarisation, noise, rotation, borders, page segmentation modes and dictionaries.

links.title: Tesseract User Manual: Command Line Usage
links.why: How the tesseract program is called, with -l for one or several languages joined by +, and what the order of languages does.

links.title: Tesseract User Manual: Traineddata Files for Version 4.00 +
links.why: The list of language and script data files, with their codes such as jpn and aze_cyrl.

links.title: NAPS2: Command Line Usage
links.why: Every option of the NAPS2 command line, including -i with its slice notation, --ocrlang and -n 0.

links.title: OCRmyPDF documentation
links.why: The package the chapter suggests when NAPS2 does not suit: it adds a text layer to scanned PDF files.

links.title: Image module: Pillow documentation
links.why: Image.open, Image.crop and the other methods used to prepare an image before recognition.

links.title: subprocess: Subprocess management
links.why: What subprocess.run returns, capture_output and check, which the chapter's NAPS2 call does not use.

links.title: Built-in Functions: open()
links.why: The modes of open(), including 'a' for appending, and the encoding argument.

links.title: ISO 639-2 Language Code List (Library of Congress)
links.why: The code list NAPS2 points to, with the two codes some languages have.
